QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_5

question.text: Hariyali Foundation invested INR 40 lakh in a watershed program. Ms. Priya Shah (SIA) computes gross present value of outcomes at INR 1.20 crore, deadweight 10%, attribution 20%, drop-off 5%, and displacement nil. What is the SROI ratio she should report?

explanation.text: The Logic: Standard SROI methodology starts from the gross present value of outcomes and applies a multiplicative cascade of standard adjustments before dividing by the investment. Starting from INR 1.20 crore: after deadweight 10% -> 1.20 x (1 - 0.10) = 1.08 crore; after attribution 20% -> 1.08 x (1 - 0.20) = 0.864 crore; after drop-off 5% -> 0.864 x (1 - 0.05) = 0.8208 crore = approximately INR 82.08 lakh; displacement is nil. SROI = Net Impact Value / Investment = 82.08 / 40 ≈ 2.05:1. A ratio above 1:1 indicates a positive net social return on the investment. The Trap: 3.00:1 simply divides gross GPV (1.20 crore) by investment (40 lakh) with no adjustments at all - the most common mistake. 2.57:1 applies only the deadweight 10% deduction. 1.80:1 over-deducts (e.g., subtracting adjustment percentages additively instead of applying them multiplicatively). The correct method is the multiplicative cascade in the order deadweight -> attribution -> drop-off -> displacement. Note: The cited workbook pages (134, 135, 151, 158 of the Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination Workbook) cover SROI, baseline / counterfactual, and the requirement to disclose calculations and assumptions, but they do not, in the pages checked, write out the SROI ratio formula or the exact deadweight-attribution-drop-off adjustment mechanics. The framing above reflects general SROI methodology as practised in social-impact evaluation, and the arithmetic is internally consistent with that methodology.
